| [NOTE-030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md) v2 | Pusey, Barrett & Rudolph, reality of the quantum state (PBR) | Take pure states \|ψ0⟩, \|ψ1⟩ with \|⟨ψ0\|ψ1⟩\| = cos θ. Assume (a) a model assigns each preparation a distribution µ_i(λ) over physical states, (b) n independent preparations yield the product distribution µ_{x1}(λ1)⋯µ_{xn}(λn), and (c) outcome probabilities depend only on (λ1, …, λn). If the model's predictions are within ε of quantum theory, then D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} for any n with 2^{1/n} − 1 ≤ tan(θ/2) (Eq. 7, App. B). At ε = 0 the distributions for distinct pure states cannot overlap on a set of non-zero measure, so Harrigan–Spekkens ψ-epistemic models are ruled out. | Read |
| [NOTE-038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md) v2 | Structural Realism (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy) | The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the lesson of theory change. | [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md) | Nagel: what is it like to be a bat | An organism is conscious if and only if there is something it is like to be it. Psychophysical reduction therefore cannot follow the usual pattern of dropping a point of view in favour of a more objective description of the same thing: for experience, that leads away from the phenomenon. Physicalism is left not refuted but not yet understandable. The closing proposal is an "objective phenomenology" of the structure of experience. | Read |

| [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) v2 | Nahas & Sachs — What's at stake in naturalizing teleology | The paper argues that "naturalizing teleology" serves at least two relatively autonomous projects with different success criteria. One is scientific: whether an organism-centred account improves biology, which requires operationalisable models that may trade truth for usefulness. The other is philosophical: whether organismal teleology reshapes the liberal-versus-scientific naturalism debate about mind in nature, which requires truth but no operationalisation. It applies the distinction to one recurring dispute, the demarcation of teleological systems from dissipative structures. In the scientific context, models "cannot and need not" demarcate (§4.1: Cusimano & Sterner; McShea & Babcock). | [NOTE-095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-095.md) v2 | Morganti — From OSR to metaphysical coherentism | Morganti argues from a survey rather than proving anything. Strong, moderate and contextualist OSR each fail as metaphysics: particle kinds have intrinsic features no group-theoretic analysis reduces, and the argument from permutation invariance is inconclusive. What OSR gets right about symmetry, entanglement and particle kinds is better captured by "metaphysical coherentism": object-like entities (in one domain) stand in symmetric *partial* ontological dependence on one another. Cycles of such dependence can be kept irreflexive, and so explanatorily non-trivial, by relaxing transitivity (quasi-transitivity) or by making only partial dependence symmetric. | Read |

| [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md) v2 | Bourrat — Reproducees, reproducers, Darwinian individuals | Bourrat builds a nested vocabulary. A reproducee is a B that comes after A, is caused by A, and is of A's relevant class. A reproducer is a reproducee with reproductive autonomy, meaning it can reproduce across a range of backgrounds. A Darwinian individual is a reproducer with high reproductive causal control, meaning heredity survives as the parent's description is made finer. On that vocabulary, genes of multicellular organisms are, like hearts, mere reproducees, but with high control. Material overlap is necessary for reproducers, which are whole life cycles, and unnecessary for reproducees, so Griesemer and Godfrey-Smith partly talk past each other. | [NOTE-118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-118.md) v2 | Belot — Time and change in mechanics | For theories with ideal existence, uniqueness and a dynamical time-translation group, time is three intertwined ℝ-actions (on spacetime, on the symplectic space of solutions, and on the isomorphic space of initial data), and change is a slicing-indexed family of functions on those spaces. Singular dynamics, gauge freedom and time-dependence each damage this picture in a repairable way. Spatially compact vacuum GR breaks it, because the reduced Hamiltonian vanishes (h ≡ 0) and there is only one canonical isomorphism between the reduced spaces. That is the problem of time. It is not an artefact of the 3+1 split, it does not show change to be illusory, and it is absent from asymptotically flat GR and from artificially generally covariant theories. A parameterized "geometric time", such as CMC, restores change and, in the CMC case, a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow. | Read |

So its time-dependence and non-uniqueness (a phase shift, a density matrix) are harmless, it counts as non-epistemic and ontic, and it can take part in constructive explanation. Each of these is argued informally, and the escape from PBR is by relabelling the ontic/epistemic distinction, not by engaging the theorem. | Read |
| [NOTE-155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-155.md) | Trappes — Defining the niche for niche construction | NCT's "evolutionary niche" (the sum of selection pressures on a population) is not a simple translation of Hutchinson's ecological niche: even against the restricted realized population niche it differs in extension, so ecological and evolutionary findings about niches cannot be transferred between the fields without checking which niche is meant. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md) | Grindrod et al. — Distributional semantics & holism | The holism of distributional/LLM meaning does not succumb to the instability objection, because what matters for communication is "differential" instability (changes in relative distances), which is constrained by frequent, consistent use and turns out to be a feature, not a bug. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-159.md) | SEP — Philosophy of microbiology | Philosophy of biology's animal-centred habits distort its conclusions: taking microbes seriously changes debates over species concepts, the tree of life, major transitions, model systems, and — through microbiome research — biological individuality and causal explanation. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md) | Cartwright — Rigour vs evidential diversity | Demanding "rigour" (as exemplified by RCTs) works against the evidential diversity that singular causal claims need; reliable predictions about whether C will cause E in a specific setting require evidencing every step of the causal process, which takes a hotchpotch of mostly non-rigorous methods. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) v2 | French — Unitary inequivalence and structural realism | French answers Howard's objection that QFT's unitarily inequivalent representations leave the structural realist with non-isomorphic, competing structures. He offers two routes. The first is to adopt cut-off "conventional" QFT with Wallace, on which the inequivalence is an artefact or harmless. The second is to follow Ruetsche's Swiss Army Knife and treat the algebra as a modal structure spanning all representations. On that reading spontaneous symmetry breaking preserves the symmetry across the degenerate vacua, and the DHR analysis derives quantum statistics from the algebra. Adding Baker's criterion, on which a symmetry mapping between representations suffices for intertranslatability, removes the assumption behind the objection, and French ends with a third option that combines the two routes. Every step is an informal argument layered on others' technical results; the paper proves nothing itself. | Read |
| [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md) | Martínez — information-processing view of representation | A state counts as a representation when it shows adaptations for transmitting information for its own sake, i.e. for efficiently trading off rate, distortion and coder complexity — and that trade-off is what grounds the properties cognitive scientists attribute to representations. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md) | Hartmann & Trpin — Coherence-based explanatory power | Probabilistic measures of explanatory power survive Lange's entailment problem and Roche & Sober's "Two Likelihood Inequalities" critique if explanatory power is measured as how well the whole set of explanantia coheres with the explanandum versus with its negation — in particular using the CohOG+ coherence measure. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-169](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-169.md) | Seth — Conscious AI and biological naturalism | Conscious AI needs both computational functionalism and enough substrate flexibility to run consciousness-relevant computations in silicon, and both are doubtful. Seth argues that positive, non-vitalist reasons from predictive processing, the free energy principle and autopoiesis tie consciousness to being alive, so real AI consciousness is unlikely on current trajectories, while conscious-*seeming* AI is nearly inevitable and ethically pressing. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md) | Takola & Schielzeth — Hutchinson's niche for individuals | A Hutchinsonian niche can be scaled down to single organisms if it is defined as the environmental conditions under which a particular individual has an expected lifetime reproductive success of at least one. Doing so forces a split between realized and potential niches, a choice among time-slice, prospective and trajectory views, and extra intraspecific dimensions. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-171.md) | Algorithmic nudging needs interdisciplinary oversight | Because AI systems can learn nudges that exploit biases nobody has documented, judging algorithmic nudges by predictive success alone repeats Friedman's instrumentalism, and Hausman's "look under the hood" rejoinder supports mandatory oversight by experts in human cognition. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-172.md) v2 | Watson — On the philosophy of unsupervised learning | Watson argues that clustering, abstraction and generative modelling each come with an epistemic thesis (EC, EA, EG — we identify natural kinds, essential properties and unrealized possibilities via such algorithms or something like them), which he accepts. Each also comes with an ontological thesis (OC, OA, OG — these just *are* what the algorithms ought to find under ideal conditions), which he rejects because nothing guarantees they are effectively computable. He adds a pragmatic, context-relative view of natural kinds, and closes with the claim that unsupervised outputs are neither "objective" nor vacuous. They should be validated by error-statistical means: resampling stability, generalization of clusters to held-out data, out-of-sample likelihood, and train-on-synthetic scores. | Read |
| [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md) v2 | Griesemer & Shavit — Scaffolding individuality (3Cs) | The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. Table 1 puts the transition to a new level of individuality between stages 2 and 3 only. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. Its one argued conclusion is hedged: community-level inheritance "seem[s] likely to evolve in tandem" with community-level individuality (§3). | Read |
| [NOTE-174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-174.md) v2 | Rovelli — The relational interpretation (RQM) | Rovelli restates RQM as an ontology of sparse relative facts, which arise in interactions and are labelled by the interacting systems. Its one technical rule is that an amplitude W(b,a) gives the probability P = \|W\|² only when a and b are relative to the same system. That rule removes the clash between P_collapse = Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and P_unitary = \|ΣᵢW(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² (eqs. 2–4). Decoherence makes some facts approximately label-independent ("stable"). ψ is a relative-state bookkeeping device, like a Hamilton–Jacobi function S. The price, which Rovelli states, is giving up "strong realism": values are not held at all times, may be held at different times for different systems, and there is no coherent global view and no quantum state of the universe. | Read |
| [NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md) v2 | Chen — Realism about the Wave Function | A survey that sorts realist readings of the non-relativistic universal wave function into four ontological readings (a field on 3N-dimensional space, a multi-field on 3-space, properties of systems as in spacetime state realism, a Hilbert-space vector), two nomological ones (strong: time-independent and simple like the classical Hamiltonian; weak: a Humean best-system variable) and Maudlin's sui generis option. It tabulates their compatibility with BM, GRW0/m/f and S0/Sm and with high- versus low-dimensional fundamental space (Table 1, 10 of 56 cells "?"), and declares no winner. | Read |
| [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md) v2 | De Haro & Butterfield — Philosophy and Physics of Duality | The book gives a formal Schema: a duality is an isomorphism between the "model roots" (state space, quantities, dynamics) of two models of a common-core bare theory, with values and dynamics matching. It pairs this with an interpretative condition: duals are physically equivalent iff (A) they are duals and (B) i1 = i2∘d. On that basis it argues four things. First, there are no genuine cases of in-principle underdetermination in the examples, and a cautious realist can commit to the common core. Second, dualities do not favour structural realism. Third, duality is formally incompatible with ontological emergence, except "beside" it (AdS/CFT's RG direction), via effective dualities, or epistemically. Fourth, quasi-dualities motivate a "geometric view" on which models are charts on a successor theory's moduli space. | Read |
| [NOTE-182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-182.md) v2 | Arsiwalla et al. — Pregeometry and formal language | A programmatic essay with no construction, theorem or model of its own. It argues that inferential justification in a materialist ontology regresses without end (§3), that a "coherentist" constructivism escapes the regress, and that Wheeler's pregeometry is therefore best read as "structureless structure": the types and compositional rules of a computational language such as homotopy type theory (§§4, 6). Every construction of space from such rules that it points to is in the authors' own earlier papers ([13, 17, 18]) or is promised as "a forthcoming publication" (fn. 1, p. 3). | Read |
| [NOTE-183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-183.md) | Birch — AI Consciousness: A Centrist Manifesto | Two challenges — users misattributing human-like consciousness to chatbots, and the real but untestable-for-now possibility of profoundly alien AI consciousness — must be met together. Birch argues this means nudging users out of the "persisting interlocutor illusion" without denying that AI could be conscious, while building research programmes, via comparative animal-consciousness science, that could test both computational-functionalist and biological-naturalist claims. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md) | SEP — Units and levels of selection | The "units of selection" debate bundles four separable research questions — interactor, replicator/reproducer, manifestor-of-adaptation and beneficiary — pursued by two multilevel schools (Wrightian evolutionary-change and Fisherian adaptationist/kin-selection) with different models, so many apparent disagreements are answers to different questions. | Skimmed |
